The basis is: فديت بنفسي ومالي نفسه ("I ransomed his self with my self and my wealth"). The meaning of ما آلوك is "I do not withhold from you"; then in the verse it was made to carry the meaning of granting, i.e. I do not grant you except what I am able to.
Of inversion in ordinary speech are «أدخلت القلنسوة في رأسي» ("I put the cap into my head"), «عرضت الناقة على الحوض» ("I presented the she-camel to the trough") and «عرضتها على الماء» ("I presented it to the water"). Of it is His words: «وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ». And Thaʿlab said concerning His words (ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُها سَبْعُونَ ذِراعاً فَاسْلُكُوهُ): the meaning is "insert a chain into him". And of it is His words (ثُمَّ دَنا فَتَدَلَّى فَكانَ قابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنى): its basis is قابي قوس ("the two lengths of a bow"), so the dual was inverted with the singular. This is good if القاب is explained as what lies between the grip of the bow and its سية (i.e. its tip); and it has two tips, so it has two قابs. A parallel to what has passed in the noble verse is the saying of Ibn al-Aʿrābī:
إذا أحسن ابن العم بعد إساءة ... فلست لشرّي فعله بحمول
(When the cousin does good after doing ill, I am not one to bear the worse of his two deeds.)
I.e. "I am not one to bear the worse of his two deeds" (لشر فعليه). And of inversion is His words: (فَعَمِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ); the basis is "so you were blind to it". And of it is His words (ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة أولي القوة): the meaning is that the band would be weighed down by them, i.e. would rise with them heavily. The upshot is that this style occurs among the Arabs and in their modes of expression, the Noble Qur'an has come with it, and it gives the meaning strength and beauty. [Translator's note: the source quotes the verse as «ما إن مفاتحه ...»; the muṣḥaf text (al-Qaṣaṣ 28:76) reads «مَا إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُ لَتَنُوأُ بِالْعُصْبَةِ أُولِي الْقُوَّةِ». The source also glosses فَعَمِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ with "فعميتم عنها" (second person). Both translated as printed.]

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {تَنزِيلٌ}: This is the reading of the majority, I mean the nominative, on the basis of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: "it is a revelation" (هو تنزيلٌ); a similar case has been discussed before. Abū al-Sammāl read «تَنْزيلاً» in the accusative, on the basis of an omitted verb, that is: "He sent down a revelation" (نَزَّل تنزيلاً).

semin-durr:44-44.t: His saying: {وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ}: This is the reading of the majority. It is the form تَفَعَّل from القول (speech), in the active voice. al-Zamakhsharī said: "التقوُّل is the form افتعال of speech, because it involves affectation on the part of the one who does the افتعال." Some read «تُقُوِّل» in the passive. If this reader made «بعضُ الأقاويل» nominative, then that is straightforward; otherwise the element standing in the place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil) is the preposition and its genitive noun. This holds according to those who permit something other than the direct object (mafʿūl bihi) to stand in for the agent even when the direct object is present. Dhakwān and his son Muḥammad read «يقولُ», the imperfect of «قال». الأقاويل is the plural of أقوال, and أقوال is the plural of قَوْل, so it parallels أباييت, the plural of أبيات, which is the plural of بيت. al-Zamakhsharī said: "He called the fabricated sayings أقاويل in order to belittle and demean them, as you say أعاجيب and أضاحيك, as though it were a plural of the form أُفْعُولة from القول."

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {باليمين}: It is permissible that the bāʾ keep its original sense and not be redundant (zāʾida), the meaning being: "We would have seized him with a strength from Us." Then the bāʾ expresses ḥāl (circumstantial), the ḥāl being from the agent, and it takes the status of a redundant one. In that case اليمين here is a figurative expression for strength and mastery. It is also permissible that it be redundant, the meaning being: "We would have seized his right hand from him." Here اليمين means the limb itself, as is done to a man who is put to death in captivity: he is seized by his right hand and struck on the neck with the sword face to face, which is harder on him. الوتين is the aorta of the heart (نياط القلب); if it is severed its owner dies. al-Kalbī said: "It is a vein between the العلباء and the throat; the two علباوان have the vein between them, and العلباء is the sinew of the neck." It was also said: it is a thick vein that the butcher's blade meets. al-Shammākh said:
4324 - إذا بَلَّغْتِني وحَملْتِ رَحْلِي ... عَرابةَ فاشْرَقي بدمِ الوتينِ
(When you have carried me, with my saddle load, to ʿArāba, then choke on the blood of your aorta.)

semin-durr:47-47.t: His saying: {حَاجِزِينَ}: There are two views. The first: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «أحد» in form, but it is in the plural by sense, because «أحداً» is general in the context of negation, like all indefinite nouns occurring in the context of negation. This was said by al-Zamakhsharī and al-Ḥūfī. On this view «منكم» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the mubtadaʾ is «مِنْ أحدٍ», in which «مِنْ» is redundant because its two conditions are met. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] weakened it, saying that the negation operates on his being "among you", whereas the meaning is the negation of preventing from that which is intended. The second: that it is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī «ما», with «مِنْ أحد» as its ism (subject), and the khabar is in the plural for the reason given above. On this view «منكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because originally it is a ṣifa (adjective) of «أحد», or it is attached to «حاجزين». This does no harm, since what depends on the khabar is a preposition with its genitive noun; if it were an explicit direct object it would be impossible. One cannot say: «ما طعامَك زيدٌ آكلاً» ("Zayd is not one who eats your food"). Or it is attached to an omitted element by way of clarification. «عنه» is attached to «حاجزين» on both views, and the pronoun refers to the one who fabricated, or to the killing indicated by His saying: «لأَخَذْنا», «لَقَطَعْنا».

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {وَإِنَّهُ لَتَذْكِرَةٌ}: that is, the Qur'an; likewise «إنه لحَسْرة». It was also said that it refers to the denial of it, because «مكذِّبين» points to the maṣdar (verbal noun), just as السفيه points to it in his saying:
4325 - إذا نُهِي السَّفيهُ جرى إليه ... وحالفَ والسَّفيهُ إلى خِلافِ
(When the fool is forbidden, he runs toward it, and he sides with it, and the fool is prone to opposition.)
that is, toward foolishness (السَّفَه).

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {الحاقة}: a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ما» is a second mubtadaʾ, and «الحاقَّةُ» is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of the first. The treatment of this has already been given in al-Wāqiʿa. There is a fine question and a fine answer there, so consult it. In «الحاقَّة» there are two possibilities. The first: it is a description, an active participle, in the sense that it exposes the realities of things. It was said: because the matter is fulfilled (yaḥiqqu) in it, so it belongs to the category of "a sleeping night" and "a fasting day". It was said: from ḥaqqa al-shayʾ, "the thing was established", so it is established and sure to occur. It was said: because it overcomes (taḥuqqu) everyone who disputes (muḥāqq) in the religion of Allah, that is, it prevails over him; from ḥāqaqtuhu fa-ḥaqaqtuhu aḥuqquhu, that is, "I overcame him." The second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like al-ʿāqiba and al-ʿāfiya.

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {مَا الحاقة}: in the position of the accusative by the removal of the preposition, because adrā with the hamza is transitive to two objects, the first by itself and the second by the bāʾ. The Exalted said: {وَلاَ أَدْرَاكُمْ بِهِ} [Yūnus: 16]. So when the interrogative clause occurs suspending it, it is in the position of the second object. Without the hamza it is transitive to one object by the bāʾ, as in "I knew of such and such" (daraytu bi-kadhā), and it may have the sense of ʿalima (to know), in which case it is transitive to two objects.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {فَأُهْلِكُواْ}: this is the reading of the majority. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «فَهَلَكوا», active, from the triliteral halaka.
His saying: {بالطاغية}, that is, by the cry that exceeded all bounds. It was said: by the transgressing deed. It was said: by the transgressing man, who is the hamstringer of the she-camel, and the hāʾ is for intensification; so on these views al-ṭāghiya is an adjective. It was said: al-ṭāghiya is a maṣdar, and this is made clear by {كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَاهَآ} [al-Shams: 11]. The bāʾ is for causation on all the views, except the first view, where it is for instrumentality, as in "I worked with the adze".

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {حُسُوماً}: there are several possibilities in it. The first: it is accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of what precedes it. The second: it is accusative as a maṣdar of a verb of its own root, that is, "it cuts them off completely" (taḥsimuhum ḥusūman). The third: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "possessing continuous cutting off". The fourth: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). This is made clear by al-Zamakhsharī's saying: "Al-ḥusūm must be either the plural of ḥāsim, like shāhid and shuhūd, or a maṣdar, like al-shukūr and al-kufūr. If it is a plural, then the meaning of His saying «حُسُوماً» is: ill-omened days that cut off every good and uprooted every blessing; or continuous in the blowing of the wind, not subsiding for an hour, as an image of their succession likened to the succession of the cauterizer's action in repeating the cautery on the sore, again and again, until it is cut off. If it is a maṣdar, then either it is accusative by its own verb, implied, that is, 'it cuts off completely', meaning 'it uproots utterly'; or it is an adjective, as in saying 'possessing cutting off'; or it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, that is, 'He subjected it against them for the purpose of uprooting.'" ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Zurāra al-Kilābī said: 4316 - ففرَّق بين بَيْنِهُمُ زمانٌ ... تتابَعَ فيه أعوامٌ حُسومُ
(Time separated them, a time in which unbroken years followed one another.)
End of quotation. Al-Mubarrad said: al-ḥusūm means separation; ḥasamtu al-shayʾ min al-shayʾ means "I separated it from it", and from it comes al-ḥusām (the sword). The poet said:
4317 - فأرسَلْتَ ريحاً دَبُوراً عقيماً ... فدارَتْ عليهمْ فكانَتْ حُسُوماً
(You sent a barren west wind; it circled around them and became a cutting-off.)
Al-Layth said: "It is ill omen: one says, 'these are the nights of al-ḥusūm', that is, they cut good off from their people." In my view these two opinions go back to the first opinion, because separation is a cutting, and likewise ill omen, since it cuts off good. The clause «سَخَّرها» may be an adjective of «ريح», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it because it has been specified by the description, or from the pronoun in «عاتية», or it may be resumptive.
His saying: {فِيهَا صرعى}: «صَرْعَى» is a ḥāl; it is the plural of ṣarīʿ, like qatīl and qatlā, and jarīḥ and jarḥā. The pronoun in «فيها» refers to the days and nights, or to the houses, or to the wind. The most evident is the first, for its nearness and because it is mentioned.
And His saying: {كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ} is a ḥāl from the people, or resumptive. Abū Nahīk read «أَعْجُزُ» on the pattern afʿul, like ḍabuʿ and aḍbuʿ. And «نخيل» was read, reported by al-Akhfash. It has already been mentioned that a generic noun may be masculine or feminine; its feminine is preferred here for the sake of the verse endings, just as its masculine was preferred for them in Sūrat al-Qamar, as was pointed out before.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {فَهَلْ ترى}: Abū ʿAmr alone assimilated the lām into the tāʾ, and this was mentioned in al-Mulk. And «مِنْ باقية» is its object, and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida). The tāʾ in «باقية» was said to be for intensification, that is, "of any remaining"; but it is better that it be an adjective of a group (firqa) or party (ṭāʾifa) and the like.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {وَمَن قَبْلَهُ}: Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read it with kasra on the qāf and fatḥa on the bāʾ, that is, "and those who are on his side". This is supported by the reading of Abū Mūsā «وَمَن تِلْقَاءَه», and Ubayy read it «ومَنْ تبعه». The rest read it with fatḥa and sukūn, as an adverbial, that is, "and those who went before him".
His saying: {بِالْخَاطِئَةِ}: either it is an adjective /, that is, "by the sinful deed or deeds", or it is a maṣdar like al-khaṭaʾ, so that it is like al-ʿāfiya and al-kādhiba.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {فِي الجارية}: the use of «الجارية» for the ship has become predominant, as in his saying: 4318 - تِسْعُونَ جاريةً في بطنِ جاريةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Ninety girls in the belly of a ship ... — [Translator's note: «جارية» here is a riddle on both senses, "girl" and "ship"; the Turkish reading likewise renders "ninety girls".])
This is one of the riddles. The Exalted said: {وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ الجوار} [al-Shūrā: 32].

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {وَتَعِيَهَآ}: the majority read it with kasra on the ʿayn and a light yāʾ; it is the imperfect of waʿā, accusative, conjoined to «لِنَجْعَلَها». Ibn Muṣarrif, and Abū ʿAmr in the transmission of Hārūn from him, and Qunbul read it with sukūn on the ʿayn, likening it to «رَحْم» and «شَهْد», even though it is not of that type, but it became in pronunciation like a faʿil whose second radical is a guttural. From Ḥamza the concealment of the kasra is reported. From ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza also there is reported a doubled yāʾ. This is a mistake attributed to them; the transmitter simply heard the two of them clarifying the vowel of the yāʾ and thought it a shadda. It was said: they treated connection as pause and so doubled the letter; this should not be given attention. From Ḥamza also, and Mūsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿAbsī, «وتَعِيْها» with sukūn on the yāʾ is reported, and there are two possibilities in it: resumption, and conjunction to the accusative. They made the yāʾ silent only because of the heaviness of the vowel on a weak letter, like the reading {تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 89], which has already been mentioned.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {وَاحِدَةٌ}: emphasis; and «نَفْخَةٌ» is a maṣdar standing in the place of the agent. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "When it was described, its being nominative became sound." End of quotation. But even if it had not been described, its being nominative would be sound, because it is a specific maṣdar, as it indicates a single occurrence; what is forbidden according to the Basrans is only making an unspecific one the deputy agent, as in "a beating was beaten" (ḍuriba ḍarbun). The majority read both in the nominative. Abū al-Sammāl read both in the accusative, as though he made the preposition and its genitive noun stand in the place of the agent, leaving the maṣdar in its original state; and he did not make the verb «نُفخَ» feminine, because the feminine is figurative, and the intervening element made it good.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
[His saying:] {وَحُمِلَتِ الأرض}: the majority read it with a light mīm, that is, "the wind, or the angels, or the Power carried it", and then it was made passive. Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission, al-Aʿmash, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ibn Miqsam read it with a doubled mīm. The doubling may be for intensification, so it does not give the verb another object; or it may be for transitivity, so it gives the verb another object, in which case the second may be omitted and the first is the deputy agent, its implied form being: "the earth and the mountains were made to carry a wind that crumbles them", because of His saying {فَقُلْ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفاً} [Ṭā Hā: 105]. It was said that the implied form is "they were made to carry angels". It is also possible that the first is the omitted one and the second is the deputy agent.
His saying: {فَدُكَّتَا}: that is, the earth and the mountains, because the two things mentioned before are meant, as in His saying: {وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ المؤمنين اقتتلوا} [al-Ḥujurāt: 9].

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {فَيَوْمَئِذٍ}: accusative by «وَقَعَتْ». And «وقعتِ الواقعةُ» requires an interpretation: that «الواقعةُ» has become a proper name by predominant usage for the Resurrection or for the great event; otherwise "the riser rose" (qāma al-qāʾim) would not be permissible, as there is no benefit in it. This was mentioned earlier in His saying {إِذَا وَقَعَتِ الواقعة} [al-Wāqiʿa: 1]. The tanwīn in «يومئذٍ» is a compensation for a clause, its implied form being: "the day when the Trumpet is blown".

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {على أَرْجَآئِهَآ}: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject). The pronoun is for the sky; it was also said: for the earth. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the difference between His saying «والمَلَكُ» and saying 'and the angels'? I say: المَلَك ('the angel') is more general than الملائكة ('the angels'). Do you not see that your saying 'There is no angel but that he is present' is more general than your saying 'There are no angels …'?" End of quote. The Shaykh said: "It is not apparent that المَلَك is more general than الملائكة, because the singular made definite with the [generic] alif and lām can at most be meant as the plural made definite [by them] — which is why exception from it is valid. So at most it is like the plural made definite by them. As for his claim that it is more general than it, by his saying 'Do you not see …' to the end, this is no proof of his claim, because «مِنْ مَلَكٍ» is an indefinite singular in a negative context on which «مِنْ» has entered, which makes it exclusively comprehensive (al-istighrāq) [Translator's note: the text has «للاستغفارق», evidently for «للاستغراق»]; so it includes every angel, and the plural falls under it because the individual is present in it, so every individual is negated. This is unlike «مِنْ ملائكة», for «مِنْ» has entered on an indefinite plural, so it is general over every plural group of angels, and it does not follow from that that every individual angel is negated. If you said 'There are no men in the house', it would be permissible that there be one in it, because the negation extends only over a plural, and the negation of the individual does not follow from the negation of the plural. And «المَلَك» in the verse is not in a negative context with «مِنْ» entering on it; it was brought in the singular only because it is lighter, and because His saying «على أَرْجائِها» indicates the plural, since one individual, as one, cannot be 'on its sides' at one time, but only at [different] times. What is meant — and Allah knows best — is that the angels are on its sides, not that one single angel moves about its sides at [different] times."
I say: al-Zamakhsharī's source for this is what I quoted from him previously at the end of Sūrat al-Baqara at His saying {وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ}, so let it be consulted there. As for the Shaykh's saying regarding "There are no men [in the house]" that the negation extends over the ranks of the plural, people have disagreement on it, and there is a point to consider in it; but the verified view is what he mentioned. The pronoun in «فوقهم» may refer back to «المَلَك», since it is in the sense of the plural as stated, or to the eight bearers. It was also said: it refers to the whole of the world, i.e. the angels carry the Throne of Allah the Exalted above the whole world.
His saying: {ثمانيةٌ}: Allah the Exalted left this number vague and did not mention a tamyīz (specification) for it. It was said: its implied form is "eight persons"; and it was said: "eight ranks".

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ}: «تُعْرَضُون» is the answer (jawāb) of «إذا» in His saying «فإذا نُفِخَ» — the Shaykh said this. There is a point to consider in it; rather, its answer is what preceded, His saying «وقَعَتِ الواقعة», and «تُعْرَضُون» on this [view] is resumptive.
His saying: {لاَ تخفى}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read it with the yāʾ from below, because the femininity is figurative, and also because of the separation; and they follow their principle in tilting (imāla) the alif. The rest read «لا تَخْفى» with the tāʾ from above, because of the grammatical femininity, and with fatḥa [no imāla], which is the basic form.
His saying: {وَاهِيَةٌ}: i.e. weak. One says وَهَى الشيءُ يَهِي وَهْياً, i.e. it became weak; and وهَى السِّقاءُ: the waterskin tore. He said:
4319 - خَلِّ سبيلَ مَنْ وَهَى سِقاؤُهُ ... ومَنْ هُرِيْقَ بالفَلاةِ ماؤُه
(Let go the one whose waterskin has torn, and whose water has been spilled in the desert.)
His saying: {أَرْجَآئِهَآ}: i.e. its sides and regions. Its singular is رَجا, with the short alif; the alif is written the reverse of رمى [i.e. as a tall alif], because they say رَجَوان. He said:
4320 - فلا يُرْمَى بِيَ الرَّجَوانِ أني ... أقَلُّ القومِ، مَنْ يُغْني مكاني
(I am not one to be cast to the two sides [i.e. disregarded] — for I am …, who can take my place?)
Another said:
4321 - كأَنْ لم تَرَيْ قبلي أسيراً مُقَيدَّاً ... ولا رجلاً يُرْمى به الرَّجَوانِ
(As if you had never seen before me a fettered captive, nor a man cast to the two sides.)

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {هَآؤُمُ}: i.e. take! There are dialectal forms in it, because it may be an explicit verb, or it may be a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), and in both cases its meaning is "take". If it is a verbal noun — and that is what is mentioned in the noble verse — there are two forms in it: with the long vowel and with the short. You say: ها درهماً يا زيدُ and هاءَ درهماً ("Take a dirham, O Zayd"). They remain so in all situations — singular, dual, plural, masculine and feminine — and the kāf of address attaches to them as it attaches to the demonstrative, agreeing with the one you address according to the actual case, as it agrees when it is his pronoun, as in: هاكَ هاءكَ، هاكِ هاءَكِ to the end. And the hamza of «هاء» takes the place of the kāf of address, inflected as the kāf of address is inflected, so you say: هاءَ يا زيدُ، وهاءِ يا هندُ، هاؤُما، هاؤُم، هاؤُنَّ — and this is the usage of the Quran.
When it is an explicit verb — because the overt nominative pronouns attach to it — there are three forms in it. The first: that it be like عاطى يُعاطي; so one says: هاءِ يا زيدُ، هائِي يا هندُ، هائِيا يا زيدان or يا هندان، هاؤُوا يا زيدون، هائِيْنَ يا هنداتُ. The second: that it be like «هَبْ», so you say: هَأْ، هَئِي، هَآ، هَؤُوا، هَأْنَ, like هَبْ، هَبِي، هَبا، هَبُوا، هَبْنَ.
The third: that it be like خَفْ, the imperative of الخوف, so one says: هَأْ، هائي، هاءا، هاؤوا، هَأْنَ, like خَفْ، خافِي، خافا، خافُوا، خَفْنَ.
There is disagreement about what it signifies. The well-known view is that it means "take". It was also said: its meaning is "come!", so it is made transitive by «إلى». It was also said: it is a word coined for answering a caller in joy and eagerness; in the ḥadīth: "A Bedouin called him in a loud voice, and the Prophet ﷺ answered him: 'هاؤُم', with the force of his voice." Of its being in the sense of "take" is the ḥadīth on usury: "except هاءَ وهاء", i.e. each of the two parties to the sale says: "Take." It was also said: its meaning is "aim for"; those [who say this] claimed that it is compounded of the ها of alerting and أمُوا from الأَمّ, which is aiming, and lightening and usage turned it into هاؤم. It was also said: the mīm is the pronoun of a group of males. Al-Qutabī claimed that the hamza is a substitute for the kāf: if he meant that it takes its place, that is correct; but if he meant technical substitution (al-badal al-ṣināʿī), it is not correct.
His saying: {هَآؤُمُ} requires an object, to which it passes over by itself if it is in the sense of "take" or "aim for", and by «إلى» if it is in the sense of "come". And «اقْرؤُوا» also requires it; so the two contend (tanāzuʿ) over «كتابِيَهْ», and the second has been given the governing, because of the omission from the first. The verification of this has preceded in Sūrat al-Kahf and elsewhere. The hāʾ in «كتابِيَهْ», «حِسابِيَهْ», «سُلْطانِيَهْ» and «مالِيَهْ» is for pausing (li-l-sakt); by right it should be dropped in continuation and retained in pause. But continuation was treated like pausing, or it was continued with the intention of pausing, in «كتابِيَهْ» and «حِسابِيَهْ» by agreement, so the hāʾ was retained; and likewise in «مالِيه», «سُلْطانِيَهْ» and «ما هِيَهْ» in {القارعة} [al-Qāriʿa: 10] according to all the readers except Ḥamza, may Allah have mercy on him, for he dropped the hāʾ from these three words in continuation and retained it in pause — because in pause it is needed to protect the vowel of the word paused on, while in continuation it is dispensed with.
If it is said: then why did he not do that in «كِتَابِيَهْ» and «حسابِيَهْ»? The answer is that he combined the two usages [Translator's note: the text has «بني», evidently for «بين»]. This is within the seven readings. Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with it dropped in all the words, in continuation and in pause, except in al-Qāriʿa, for no transmission from him regarding it has been verified. Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with it dropped in them in continuation and retained in pause. Ibn Muḥayṣin makes the yāʾ quiescent in the words mentioned in continuation. The truth is that it is a sound reading — I mean the retention of the hāʾ of pausing in continuation — because it is present in the script of the noble Muṣḥaf. So no attention is paid to the saying of al-Zahrāwī: "Retaining it in continuation is a solecism (laḥn); I know no one who permits it." The discussion of the hāʾ of pausing has preceded in al-Baqara and al-Anʿām more fully than this, so take note of it.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {رَّاضِيَةٍ}: there are three possibilities in it. The first: it is figurative; the life is made "pleased" because of its place and its reaching those who deserve it, or because there is no state more perfect than its state. The second: it is by relation (nisba), that is, "possessing contentment", like lābin and tāmir. The third: it is one of those in which a fāʿil has the sense of a mafʿūl, as in {مِن مَّآءٍ دَافِقٍ} [al-Ṭāriq: 6], that is, madfūq (poured), just as a mafʿūl has come in the sense of a fāʿil, as in His saying: {حِجَاباً مَّسْتُوراً} [al-Isrāʾ: 45], that is, sātir (concealing); this has already been mentioned.

semin-durr:23-23.t: And al-quṭūf is the plural of qiṭf, which is a fiʿl with the sense of a mafʿūl, like al-riʿy and al-dhibḥ; it is what the picker picks of fruits.

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {كُلُواْ}: that is, "it will be said to them: eat." And «هَنيئاً» was discussed at the beginning of al-Nisāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed here that it be accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "pleasant eating" and "pleasant drinking", and that it be accusative as a maṣdar by an implied operator of its own root, that is, "may you enjoy that pleasantly" (hanʾtum bi-dhālika hanīʾan). In «بما أَسْلَفْتُم» the bāʾ is causal, and «ما» is either a maṣdar particle or a noun.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {مَآ أغنى}: it may be a negation, and it may be an interrogative of reproach addressed to himself.

semin-durr:30-30.t: And His saying: {خُذُوهُ} is like His saying {كُلُواْ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 24] in the implication of "saying". And His saying {ثُمَّ الجحيم صَلُّوهُ}: the fronting of the object gives exclusivity according to some of them; for that reason al-Zamakhsharī said: "then do not roast him except in the Blazing Fire." The Shaykh said: "What he said is not the doctrine of Sībawayh nor of the skilled grammarians." I say: this question has already been dealt with thoroughly, and the words of the grammarians do not reject what he said.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ}: in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «سِلْسِلَةٍ». And «في سِلْسِلَة» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «اسْلُكوه»; the fāʾ does not prevent that. الذِّراع ("cubit") is feminine; that is why it is pluralised on afʿul and the tāʾ is dropped from its number. He said:
432 - 2- أَرْمي عليها وهي فَرْعٌ أَجْمَعُ ... وهي ثلاثُ أَذْرُعٍ وإصبعُ
(I shoot with it, and it is an unspliced branch, whole; it is three cubits and a finger.) [Translator's note: the verse number is printed thus in the text; 4322 is evidently meant.]
Some of them claimed that in His saying «في سِلْسلة» «فاسلكوه» there is an inversion (qalb). He said: because it is transmitted in the tafsīr that the chain enters by his mouth and comes out by his rear, so it is what is inserted into him, not he who is inserted into it. What is apparent is that this is not needed, because it is related that, owing to its length, it is placed on his neck and coiled around him until it surrounds him on all sides, so he is the one inserted into it, since it surrounds him.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning of placing the chain before the inserting is like that of placing Hellfire before the roasting, i.e. do not insert him except into this chain. And «ثُمَّ» is to indicate the disparity between the shackling and roasting in Hellfire, and what precedes it, and the inserting into the chain — not to indicate a lapse of time." The Shaykh disputed with him, as is his habit, over the placing first conveying restriction (ikhtiṣāṣ), and the answer to that is what has preceded. He also disputed with him over «ثُمَّ» indicating a lapse in rank, and said: "A temporal lapse is possible: that he be roasted after being inserted, and inserted after being seized and shackled, with an interval between these things." End of quote. There is a point to consider in this, inasmuch as threatening with the punishment coming in succession is more emphatic and more decisive than threatening with it spread out.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying [Translator's note: the text has «وقله», evidently for «وقوله»]: {وَلاَ يَحُضُّ}: الحضّ is urging to an action and being eager for its occurrence. From it are the particles of incitement (ḥurūf al-taḥḍīḍ), to which a chapter is given in grammar, because by them the occurrence and bringing about of the action is sought.

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {فَلَيْسَ لَهُ اليوم هَا هُنَا حَمِيمٌ}: there are two views on the khabar (predicate) of «ليس». The first: «له»; the second: «ههنا». Whichever of them is the khabar, the other is attached to it, or is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «حميمٌ». «اليومَ» may not be the khabar at all, because it is a time, while what is spoken of is a concrete entity (juththa). Al-Mahdawī prohibited «ههنا» from being the khabar, without mentioning what prevents it. Al-Qurṭubī mentioned it, saying: "Because the meaning would become: there is no food here except from ghislīn, and that is not sound, because there is other food there." End of quote. There is a point to consider in this, because we do not concede, firstly, that there is other food there. If he meant His saying {لَّيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلاَّ مِن ضَرِيعٍ} [al-Ghāshiya: 6] — that this is another food than ghislīn — the answer is that some held that ghislīn is ḍarīʿ itself, which He called ghislīn in one verse and ḍarīʿ in another. And even if we concede that they are two foods, the restriction is with respect to those who eat: meaning that the food of this eater is restricted to ghislīn, which does not preclude there being another food in the Fire. If we say that «له» is the khabar, and that «اليوم» and «ههنا» are attached to what it is attached to, there is no difficulty. Likewise if we make «ههنا» the khabar and attach the preposition phrase and the adverb to it; the governor's being abstract (maʿnawī) does no harm, because of the latitude allowed with adverbs and prepositions.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ}: an adjective of «طعامٌ»; the restriction has entered on the adjective, as in your saying: "I have no man except of Banū Tamīm". What is meant by «الحميم» is the friend; on this [view] the adjective is specific to the food, i.e. he has no friend to benefit him, nor any food except from such-and-such. It was also said: the implied form is "he has no ḥamīm except from ghislīn, nor food" — Abū al-Baqāʾ said this — so he made «مِنْ غِسْلين» an adjective of «الحميم», as if he meant by it the thing with which the body is scalded, of the pus of the Fire. Then he said: "It was also said: [it is] of the food and drink, since all of it is 'tasted', as shown by His saying {وَمَن لَّمْ يَطْعَمْهُ} [al-Baqara: 249]. On this [view] {إِلاَّ مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ} is an adjective of «حميم» and of «طعام», and what is meant by «الحميم» is what is drunk." What is apparent is that the khabar (predicate) of «ليس» is His saying «مِنْ غِسْلين» when «الحميم» is taken to mean what is drunk, i.e. he has no drink and no food except ghislīn. But if «الحميم» is taken to mean the friend, that does not work. On what I have mentioned, one may ask to what the preposition phrase and the two adverbs are attached. The answer: they are attached to what the khabar is attached to; or «له» or «ههنا» is made a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «حميم», and «اليوم» is attached to what the ḥāl is attached to. «اليومَ» may not be a ḥāl of «حميم», with «له» and «ههنا» attached to what the ḥāl is attached to, because it is an adverb of time while the owner of the ḥāl is a concrete entity. This place is a fine and useful one, so reflect on it.
And «الغِسْلِين» is a fiʿlīn form from الغُسالة ("washing water"), so its nūn and yāʾ are augments. The lexicographers said: it is what flows from wounds when they are washed. In the tafsīr: it is the pus of the people of the Fire. It was also said: a tree that they eat.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {لاَّ يَأْكُلُهُ إِلاَّ الخاطئون}: an adjective of «غِسْلين». The majority pronounce «الخاطِئُون» with the hamza; it is an active participle from خَطِىءَ يَخْطأ, when someone does what is not right deliberately, whereas المُخْطِىء is one who does it without intending.
Al-Zuhrī, al-ʿAtakī, Ṭalḥa and al-Ḥasan read «الخاطِيُون» with a yāʾ with ḍamma instead of the hamza; something like it has preceded in «مُسْتَهْزِيُون» at the beginning of this work [Translator's note: literally "this subject" (الموضوع); the reference is evidently to the beginning of the book, in al-Baqara]. Nāfiʿ in one transmission, his teacher, and Shayba read it with a ṭāʾ with ḍamma and without hamza. There are two views on it. The first: that it is like the reading of the majority, except that it is lightened by omission. The second: that it is an active participle from خطا يخطو, when one follows the steps of another, so it is from His saying {لاَ تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَاتِ الشيطان} [al-Nūr: 21] — al-Zamakhsharī said this. It has passed at the beginning of this work that Nāfiʿ reads «الصابِييْنَ» without hamza, and what people transmitted concerning it has preceded. From Ibn ʿAbbās: "What are al-khāṭūn? All of us step (nakhṭū)!" And Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī related from him: "What are al-khāṭūn? It is only al-khāṭiʾūn; and what are al-ṣābūn? It is only al-ṣābiʾūn."

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ}: something like it has preceded at the end of al-Wāqiʿa, where I treated the matter in full; except that it has been said here that «لا» negates the verb of swearing, as if it were said: I do not need to swear to this, because it is a manifest truth that needs no oath. Had this been said in al-Wāqiʿa, it would have been good.

semin-durr:40-40.t: His saying: {إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ}: it is the answer to the oath.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ}: conjoined to the answer, so it is an answer [too]. He swore to two things, one affirmed and the other negated, and this is of splendid eloquence.
His saying: {قَلِيلاً مَّا تُؤْمِنُونَ} {قَلِيلاً مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ}: «قليلاً» in both places is accusative as the adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or [noun of] time, i.e. a little belief, or a little time. What puts it in the accusative is «تُؤْمِنون» and «تَذَكَّرون», and «ما» is redundant (mazīda) for emphasis. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«قليلاً» is put in the accusative by an implied verb indicated by «تُؤْمِنون». And «ما» may be negative, so their belief is negated altogether; or it may be maṣdariyya and is qualified by littleness, so it is belief in the lexical sense, because they did believe in a few things that availed them nothing, since they used to believe that the good, the keeping of family ties and the chastity which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded were true and right." The Shaykh said: "As for his saying that «قليلاً» is put in the accusative by a verb, etc., it is not sound, because [regarding] that verb indicated by «تُؤْمنون»: either «ما» is negative [or maṣdariyya], as he held. If it is negative, then that implied verb indicated by «تُؤْمِنون», negated by «ما», would be negated, so the implied form would be: 'you do not believe a little, you do not believe' — and the verb negated by «ما» may not be omitted, nor may «ما» be omitted; «زيداً ما أَضْرِبُه» is not permissible in the sense of 'I do not strike Zayd, I do not strike him'. If it is maṣdariyya, it is either in the position of the nominative by «قليلاً» as its agent, i.e. 'little is your belief' — and then «قليلاً» is left with nothing preceding it on which it could lean so as to govern, and with nothing to put it in the accusative; or in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), so it would be a mubtadaʾ without a khabar (predicate), since what precedes it is accusative."
I say: by the indication of «تُؤْمنون» of the omitted verb, Ibn ʿAṭiyya does not mean the indication mentioned in the chapter of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), such that the overt governor would explain the implied governor; rather he means mere verbal indication. So the Shaykh's objection against him, by his example «زيداً ما أَضْرِبُه», i.e. "I do not strike Zayd, I do not strike him", does not apply.
As for the second refutation, it is evident. This saying of Ibn ʿAṭiyya has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, and I discussed it with him there. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Littleness is in the sense of non-existence, i.e. you do not believe and do not take heed at all." The Shaykh said: "Pure negation is not meant by «قليلاً» here, as he claimed. That happens only in «أقَلّ», as in 'Few a man says that except Zayd' [أقَلُّ رجلٍ يقولُ ذلك إلاَّ زيدٌ], and in «قَلَّ», as in 'Seldom does a man say that except Zayd' [قَلَّ رجلٌ يقولُ ذلك إلاَّ زيدٌ]. It is sometimes used in قليل and قليلة, but only when they are nominative, as they allowed in his saying:
4323 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... قليلٌ بها الأصواتُ إلاَّ بُغامُها
(… few are the sounds in it, except her [the she-camel's] soft grunting.)
But when it is accusative, as in «قليلاً ضَرَبْتُ» ("little did I strike") or «قليلاً ما ضَرَبْتُ» with «ما» as maṣdariyya, that is not permissible; because in «قليلاً ضربْتُ» it is accusative by «ضربْتُ», and the Arabs did not use «قليلاً», when put in the accusative by the verb, as a negation, but rather as the counterpart of «كثير». And in «قليلاً ما ضربْتُ» with «ما» maṣdariyya, «قليل» would need to be nominative, because the maṣdariyya «ما» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ." End of his refutation — and it is a mere claim.
Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir — with disagreement from Ibn Dhakwān — read «يؤمنون» and «يَذَّكَّرون» in the third person, construing them with His saying «الخاطِئون»; the rest read them in the second person, construing them with «بما تُبْصِرون وما لا تُبْصرون». Ubayy read «تتذكَّرون» with two tāʾs.

ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الْحَاقَّةُ (١) مَا الْحَاقَّةُ (٢) وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحَاقَّةُ (٣))
His saying (الْحَاقَّةُ): it is said: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). It is also said: it is a mubtadaʾ and what follows it is the khabar, as mentioned in al-Wāqiʿa. And the second (مَا) is a mubtadaʾ, and «أَدْرَاكَ» the khabar; the clause after it is in the position of the accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَهَا أُذُنٌ وَاعِيَةٌ (١٢))
His saying (وَتَعِيَهَا): it is conjoined (maʿṭūf), i.e. "and so that it may retain it". Whoever made the ʿayn vowelless [وَتَعْيَهَا] avoided the kasra, as in فَخْذٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ (١٣))
(وَاحِدَةً) is a tawkīd (emphasis), because a blast can only be one.

ukberi-tibyan:14-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَحُمِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَاحِدَةً (٢٤) فَيَوْمَئِذٍ وَقَعَتِ الْوَاقِعَةُ (٢٥) وَانْشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ فَهِيَ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاهِيَةٌ (٢٦))
(وَحُمِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ): with a light [mīm]. It has also been read with doubling [وَحُمِّلَتِ], i.e. "the terrors were laid upon it".
And (يَوْمَئِذٍ) is an adverb (ẓarf) for «وَقَعَتْ», and (يَوْمَئِذٍ) [the second] is an adverb for «وَاهِيَةٌ».
«[Translator's note: the verse numbers in the source's heading, (٢٤)–(٢٦), are in error; these are verses 14–16.]»

ukberi-tibyan:19-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هَاؤُمُ اقْرَءُوا كِتَابِيَهْ (١٩) إِنِّي ظَنَنْتُ أَنِّي مُلَاقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ (٢٠) فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ (٢١))
And (هَاؤُمُ) is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) meaning "take!". And (كِتَابِيَهْ) is accusative, governed by اقْرَءُوا, not by «هَاؤُمُ», according to the Basrans; and by هَاؤُمُ according to the Kufans.
And (رَاضِيَةٍ) has three views. The first: it is in the sense of مَرْضِيَّةٍ (pleasing), like دَافِقٍ in the sense of مَدْفُوقٍ.
The second: it is on the pattern of relation (nasab), i.e. "possessing pleasure", like لَابِنٍ and تَامِرٍ.
The third: it keeps its proper sense; it is as if the life were pleased with its place and with being with the one who deserves it, or [it means] that there is no state more perfect than its state; so it is figurative.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا أَغْنَى عَنِّي مَالِيَهْ (٢٨))
His saying (مَا أَغْنَى عَنِّي): it may be negation or interrogation. The hāʾ in these places is for showing the vowel (hāʾ al-sakt), so that the verse endings agree.

ukberi-tibyan:31-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ (٣١) ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًا فَاسْلُكُوهُ (٣٢))
And (الْجَحِيمَ) is accusative by an omitted verb.
And (ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ) is an adjective (ṣifa) of سِلْسِلَةٍ. And «فِي» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «اسْلُكُوهُ», and the fāʾ did not prevent that; the implied form is "then insert him", and «ثُمَّ» is for ordering the report of what was said shortly before, without any lapse of time.

ukberi-tibyan:35-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هَاهُنَا حَمِيمٌ (٣٥) وَلَا طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ (٣٦))
The nūn in «غِسْلِينَ» is redundant (zāʾida), because it is the washings of the people of the Fire.
It is also said: the implied form is "he has no hot drink except from غِسْلِينَ, nor food".
It is also said: the exception is from both food and drink, because all of it is "tasted" (yuṭʿam), as evidenced by His saying (وَمَنْ لَمْ يَطْعَمْهُ). As for the khabar (predicate) of لَيْسَ, it is «هَاهُنَا» or «لَهُ»; whichever of them is the khabar, the other is either a ḥāl (circumstantial) from حَمِيمٌ or governed by the khabar. «الْيَوْمَ» cannot be the khabar, because it is a time, and the noun [of لَيْسَ] is a concrete entity.

ukberi-tibyan:41-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا مَا تُؤْمِنُونَ (٤١) وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا مَا تَذَكَّرُونَ (٤٢) تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٤٣))
And (قَلِيلًا) has been mentioned in al-Aʿrāf, and (تَنْزِيلٌ) in Yā Sīn.

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ (٤٥))
And (بِالْيَمِينِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَخَذْنَا, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent; it is also said: from the object.

ukberi-tibyan:47-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَاجِزِينَ (٤٧) وَإِنَّهُ لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ (٤٨))
His saying (فَمَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ): «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), and «أَحَدٍ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); there are two views on the khabar (predicate).
The first: it is «حَاجِزِينَ»; it was made plural according to the meaning of أَحَد, and made genitive according to the wording of أَحَد.
It is also said: it is accusative by مَا, and «مِنْكُمْ» was not counted as a separation; on this view «مِنْكُمْ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أَحَدٍ; it is also said: it is for clarification (tabyīn).
The second: the khabar is «مِنْكُمْ», and «عَنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to حَاجِزِينَ. The hāʾ in «إِنَّهُ» refers to the Mighty Qur'an.
«[Translator's note: حَاجِزِينَ is accusative in the Qur'anic text; the source's statement that it was "made genitive according to the wording of أَحَد" is translated as written.]»

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطَّاغِيَةِ (٥))
And (الطَّاغِيَةِ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الْعَافِيَة. It is also said: it is an active participle in the sense of "the excessive (الزَّائِدَة)".

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا فَتَرَى الْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَى كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ (٧))
(سَخَّرَهَا) is resumptive, or an adjective (ṣifa). And «حُسُومًا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "cutting them off"; it is also said: it is a plural, i.e. "consecutive". And (صَرْعَى) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «كَأَنَّهُمْ» is another ḥāl, from the pronoun in صَرْعَى.
And (خَاوِيَةٍ) follows the dialect of those who treat النَّخْل as feminine.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَهَلْ تَرَى لَهُمْ مِنْ بَاقِيَةٍ (٨))
And (بَاقِيَةٍ) is a naʿt (adjective), i.e. "a remaining state". It is also said: it is in the sense of بَقِيَّةٍ (a remnant).

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَنْ قَبْلَهُ وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَاتُ بِالْخَاطِئَةِ (٩))
And (مَنْ قَبْلَهُ), i.e. "those who preceded him in disbelief"; and (مَنْ قِبَلَهُ) [with kasra], i.e. "those with him and among his company".
And (بِالْخَاطِئَةِ), i.e. "they came with the deed possessing error", on the pattern of relation (nasab), like تَامِرٍ and لَابِنٍ.
«[Translator's note: the source writes both readings identically as قَبْلَهُ; the second must be the variant reading قِبَلَهُ, and is rendered so here.]»

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ḥāqqa
Meccan
﷽
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿الحاقَّةُ﴾ ﴿ما الحاقَّةُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 2] ("The Inevitable Reality! What is the Inevitable Reality?"). The first is nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); «ما» is also nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the second «الحاقَّةُ» is the khabar (predicate) of «ما». The [element] referring back to «ما» is the second «الحاقَّةُ», on the implied sense "What is it?" The meaning is to magnify its importance, while the wording is that of a question, as when you say: «زَيْدٌ، ما هُوَ؟» ("Zayd — what is he?!"), in the sense of magnifying his standing, whether in praise or in blame. «الحاقَّة» is the Hour and the Resurrection; it was called «الحاقَّة» because it makes real (taḥiqqu) everything a person does, good or evil. Likewise ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما الحاقَّةُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 3] ("And what will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?") means: "What thing has made you know what the Inevitable Reality is?" The position of «ما» is nominative even though it comes after «أدْراكَ», because what is in the form of a question is not governed by what precedes it; the meaning is: "What has made you know what thing the Inevitable Reality is?!"

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنّا لَمّا طَغى الماءُ حَمَلْناكم في الجارِيَةِ﴾ ("When the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship"). The meaning of «طَغى الماءُ» is: it swelled and rose. The meaning of «الجارِيَة» is: the ship of Noah (peace be upon him), and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿لِنَجْعَلَها لَكم تَذْكِرَةً﴾ ("that We might make it a reminder for you") means: that We might make this deed a reminder for you, i.e. the drowning of the people of Noah and the rescue of him and the believers with him.
And His saying: ﴿وَتَعِيَها أُذُنٌ واعِيَةٌ﴾ ("and that a retaining ear might retain it") means: an ear that keeps what it has heard and acts upon it, i.e. so that the hearer keeps what he has heard and acts upon it. Of everything you keep within yourself you say «قَدْ وعَيْتُهُ»; one says «قَدْ وعَيْتُ العِلْمَ» ("I have retained the knowledge") and «وَعَيْتُ»; and of what you keep in something other than yourself you say «أوْعَيْتُهُ»; one says «أوْعَيْتُ المَتاعَ في الوِعاءِ» ("I put the goods away in the container").
[Translator's note: the source has «و"وَعَيْتُ"، قُلْتَ وتَقُولُ», which appears garbled; translated as far as it is intelligible.]

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا نُفِخَ في الصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ واحِدَةٌ﴾ ("Then when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast"). The reading is with the nominative in ﴿نَفْخَةٌ﴾, as [the subject of a verb] whose agent is not named (i.e. nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). Al-Akhfash mentioned «نَفْخَةً واحِدَةً» in the accusative, and did not mention whether it was read so or not. It is permissible in Arabic on the basis that your saying «فِي الصُّورِ» stands in place of the deputy agent; you say «فِي الصُّورِ نَفْخًا», so «فِي الصُّورِ» is genitive in its wording, and the meaning is "the Trumpet was blown with a single blast" — this is for whoever puts «نَفْخَةً واحِدَةً» in the accusative. Whoever puts it in the nominative, it is on the meaning: "a single blast was blown in the Trumpet". As for the masculine «نُفِخَ»: had it been «نُفِخَتْ في الصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ» it would have been permissible; [but the masculine is used] because it is a non-real feminine, so making it masculine is permissible, since «النَّفْخَة» and «النَّفْخ» have one meaning. Similar to it is ﴿فَمَن جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِن رَبِّهِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 275] ("So whoever an admonition from his Lord comes to"); the meaning is the meaning of «الوَعْظ» (admonishing), while He said in another place: ﴿قَدْ جاءَتْكم مَوْعِظَةٌ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [Yūnus: 57] ("There has come to you an admonition from your Lord").

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿وانْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ فَهي يَوْمَئِذٍ واهِيَةٌ﴾ ("And the sky will be split, for that Day it will be frail"). Of anything that has become very weak one says «قَدْ وهى، فَهو واهٍ». And «وِاهِيَةٌ» is also permissible, with imāla (inclination) of the alif and the wāw because of the kasra of the hāʾ.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿والمَلَكُ عَلى أرْجائِها﴾ ("And the angels will be on its edges"): the meaning is "the angels on its sides". The rajā of everything is its side; it is a maqṣūr noun (ending in short alif), its dual is «رَجَوانِ» and its plural «أرْجاء».
﴿وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهم يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمانِيَةٌ﴾ ("And eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them that Day"): it is narrated: eight angels, their feet in the depths of the seventh earth and the Throne above their heads, while they, with heads bowed, glorify [Allah].
﴿فَأمّا مَن أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هاؤُمُ اقْرَءُوا كِتابِيَهْ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 19] ("As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: Here, read my record!"): it is narrated: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, creation will be presented three times: in two of them there will be argument, excuse-making and rebuke, and in the third the records will be scattered, and the successful one will take his record in his right hand and the ruined one his record in his left." ﴿هاؤُمُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 19] is an imperative for a group, equivalent to «هاكُمْ» ("here, take!"). You say to one man «هاءَ يا رَجُلُ», to two «هاؤُما يا رَجُلانِ», to three «هاؤُمُ يا رِجالُ», to a woman «هاءِ يا امْرَأةُ» with kasra on the hamza, to two [women] «هاؤُما», and to a group of women «هاؤُنَّ». There are three dialectal forms of this, which I have mentioned in a book other than [this] book on the Qur'an.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿إنِّي ظَنَنْتُ أنِّي مُلاقٍ حِسابِيَهْ﴾ ("Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account") means: "I was certain that I would be brought to account and raised." As for «كِتابِيَهْ» and «حِسابِيَهْ», the proper way is to pause on these hāʾs and not to read them in connection, because they were brought in for the pause. Some people dropped them in connected reading, but I do not like to contradict the Muṣḥaf, nor to read with the hāʾ retained in connected reading. These are verse-endings, so the proper way is to pause at them; and likewise His saying: ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 10] ("And what will make you know what it is?").

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ﴾ ("its clusters hanging near") means: they draw near to whoever wants them; neither distance nor thorns prevent him from reaching them.
And His saying: ﴿فِي الأيّامِ الخالِيَةِ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 24] ("in the days gone by") means: in the days that passed for them.
His saying: ﴿صَلُّوهُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 31] ("burn him"): the meaning is "make him roast in the Fire".

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ﴾ ("my authority has perished from me") means: "my argument has gone from me". «السُّلْطان» is the argument (ḥujja); likewise rulers were called «سَلاطِين», because they are the ones by whom the argument and rights are upheld.

zajjaj:36-36.t: His saying ﴿مِن غِسْلِينٍ﴾ ("of ghislīn") means: of the pus of the people of the Fire; its derivation is from what is washed off (yanghasilu) their bodies.

zajjaj:4-4.t: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned those who denied the Inevitable Reality, the Hour, the matter of the raising and the Resurrection, and what befell them, as an admonition to the community of Muḥammad ﷺ, and said: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وعادٌ بِالقارِعَةِ﴾ ("Thamūd and ʿĀd denied the Striking Calamity"), i.e. the Resurrection.

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿قَلِيلا ما تُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("little is it that you believe") and ﴿قَلِيلا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 42] ("little is it that you take heed"): «ما» is emphatic and is void (laghw) as regards i'rab; the meaning is «قَلِيلًا تُؤْمِنُونَ» and «قَلِيلًا تَذَكَّرُونَ».

zajjaj:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿تَنْـزِيلٌ مِن رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ ("A revelation from the Lord of the worlds"): it is nominative by an implied «هُوَ» ("it is"), indicated by His saying ﴿وَما هو بِقَوْلِ شاعِرٍ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 41] ("and it is not the word of a poet"), i.e. "It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds."

zajjaj:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنا بَعْضَ الأقاوِيلِ﴾ ("And had he fabricated against Us some sayings"): He means by it the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
﴿لأخَذْنا مِنهُ بِاليَمِينِ﴾ ("We would have seized him by the right hand"), i.e. with power and strength. Al-Shammākh said:
؎إذا ما رايَةٌ رُفِعَتْ لِمَجْدٍ ∗∗∗ تَلَقّاها عَرابَةٌ بِاليَمِينِ
(Whenever a banner is raised for glory, ʿArāba receives it with the right hand.)

zajjaj:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنا مِنهُ الوَتِينَ﴾ ("then We would have cut his aorta"): «الوَتِين» is the main artery by which the heart is suspended (niyāṭ al-qalb).

zajjaj:47-47.t: ﴿فَما مِنكم مِن أحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ﴾ ("And none of you could have shielded him"): «حاجِزِينَ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أحَد», and «أحَد» here has the meaning of "all"; the meaning is: "There is no group among you who could hold [Us] back from him."

zajjaj:5-5.t:
﴿فَأمّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطّاغِيَةِ﴾ ("As for Thamūd, they were destroyed by al-ṭāghiya"). The meaning of ﴿بِالطّاغِيَةِ﴾ according to the lexicographers is: by their transgression (ṭughyān); the pattern fāʿila sometimes comes with the meaning of maṣdars (verbal nouns), such as «عافِيَة» (well-being) and «عاقِبَة» (outcome). But what the meaning of the verse points to — and Allah knows best — is that they were destroyed by the overwhelming (ṭāghiya) earthquake, just as He said: ﴿وَأمّا عادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عاتِيَةٍ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 6] ("And as for ʿĀd, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind"). Of a mighty thing one says «عاتٍ» and «عاتِيَة»; likewise they were destroyed by the ṭāghiya. The evidence for describing a mighty thing with ṭughyān is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنّا لَمّا طَغى الماءُ حَمَلْناكم في الجارِيَةِ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 11] ("When the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship"); He described the water with ṭughyān because it exceeded the measure in abundance. So likewise they were destroyed by the ṭāghiya, and Allah knows best.
And His saying: ﴿بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عاتِيَةٍ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 6] means: by a wind of very intense cold. «الصَّرْصَر» is intensity of cold, and «صَرْصَر» is [a wind] in which the cold repeats itself — just as you say «قَلْقَلْتُ الشَّيْءَ» and «أقْلَلْتُ الشَّيْءَ» when you lift a thing from its place, except that «قَلْقَلْتُهُ» means I moved it back and forth, i.e. I lifted it repeatedly, whereas «أقْلَلْتُهُ» means I lifted it, and there is no indication of repetition in it. Likewise «صَرْصَر» and «صَرّ», «صَلْصَل» and «صَلّ»: when you hear the sound of creaking not repeated, you say «قَدْ صَرَّ» and «صَلَّ»; and when you mean that the sound was repeated, you say «قَدْ صَلْصَلَ» and «صَرْصَرَ».

zajjaj:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَحَقُّ اليَقِينِ﴾ ("And indeed it is the truth of certainty"): the meaning is that the Qur'an, as certainty, is the very truth of certainty.

zajjaj:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ العَظِيمِ﴾ ("So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great"): «التَّسْبِيح» means declaring Allah free of evil, and declaring Him, the Exalted, transcendent.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿سَخَّرَها عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيالٍ وثَمانِيَةَ أيّامٍ حُسُومًا﴾ ("He imposed it upon them for seven nights and eight days, ḥusūman"). The meaning of ﴿سَخَّرَها عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ is: He kept it upon them as He willed. The meaning of ﴿حُسُومًا﴾ is "continuous", and they also said "successive". As for what the language requires, it is in the sense of "cutting them off completely (taḥsimuhum ḥusūman)", i.e. carrying them away and annihilating them.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كَأنَّهم أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ خاوِيَةٍ﴾ ("as though they were the trunks of hollow palm trees"): «أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ» are the stumps of palm trees. «خاوِيَةٍ» was said of the palm trees because «نَخْل» is treated as both masculine and feminine; one says «هَذا نَخْلٌ حَسَنٌ» and «هَذِهِ نَخْلٌ حَسَنَةٌ». So «خاوِيَةٍ» is on the feminine, and He said in another place: ﴿أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ﴾ [al-Qamar: 20] ("the trunks of uprooted palm trees").

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿وَجاءَ فِرْعَوْنُ ومَن قَبْلَهُ﴾ ("And Pharaoh came, and those before him"). It was also read «وَمَن قِبَلَهُ». Whoever says «وَمَن قِبَلَهُ», its meaning is: and his followers; and whoever says «وَمَن قَبْلَهُ», the meaning is: those who preceded him. ﴿والمُؤْتَفِكاتُ بِالخاطِئَةِ﴾ ("and the overturned cities, with sin"): «المُؤْتَفِكات» are those who were overturned (iʾtufikū) for their sins, i.e. destroyed for their sins, the greatest of which was ifk — lying concerning the matter of Allah — in that they disbelieved and denied the messengers; therefore they were called «مُؤْتَفِكُون». Likewise those with whom the earth was overturned (iʾtafakat), i.e. who were swallowed by it: its meaning is simply that it turned over with them, just as the liar turns the truth over into falsehood. The meaning of ﴿بِالخاطِئَةِ﴾ is: with the great error. The evidence that lying was among their greatest sins is His saying: ﴿فَعَصَوْا رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأخَذَهم أخْذَةً رابِيَةً﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 10] ("And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with an ever-increasing seizure"), because they denied their messengers. ﴿أخْذَةً رابِيَةً﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 10]: the meaning of ﴿رابِيَةً﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 10] is: exceeding [other] events.
